# Odette Pullen

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c28 P7](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0007), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v4 c2 P10](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0010)</sub>

## Appearance

Odette is tidy, unadorned, and has a rosy-faced appearance with plump hands. At her wedding, she wore an extensive array of white satin, tulle, lace, roses, orange blossoms, and large diamond jewels.

_Sources: [v3 c2 P4](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0004), [v3 c39 P20](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0020), [v3 c41 P9](../source/v03-c41.md#nw-v03-c41-p0009), [v4 c2 P10](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0010)_

## Personality

Odette is an unassuming, steady, sensible, and dutiful individual known for her unshakeable composure and lady-like demeanor. Though pragmatic and unpretentious, she possesses a tranquil, pleasant, and gentle disposition that leaves her well-liked by others. She tends to avoid saying anything that might hurt the feelings of those around her.

_Sources: [v1 c31 P30](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0030), [v1 c32 P18](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0018), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v2 c4 P8](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0008), [v2 c7 P8](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0008), [v2 c26 P59](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0059), [v3 c2 P4](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0004), [v4 c2 P10](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0010)_

## History

During her youth in Brierley, Odette was saved by her father Gorham Pullen from nearly drowning in the Lake of Glassy Waters while gathering water lilies. She attended school under Mr. Pidgeon and was active in games and plays with her circle of friends, as well as the local Story Club. Odette attended Regent's Academy alongside several Brierley scholars, excelling in domestic science and earning a Second Class teacher's license. Upon graduating, she accepted a teaching position in Stonebridge, where she became well-regarded and earned a spot on the Inspector's Roll of Honor, though she privately found teaching tedious. As a member of the Brierley Village Improvement Society, she served on committees, including the Delford road fundraising path and visiting Judson Tibbs for moral support. She later gave up her Stonebridge post and traveled West to teach on the western prairies. While living in the West, she met Mr. Inglis, a wealthy man from Winnipeg, and returned to Brierley to marry him in a grand wedding before moving to Winnipeg.
